days.headline: Today you decide. Tomorrow it gets built.
days.line: No idea is perfect. Don't ideate too long.
intro: For way too long I thought founders had something I didn't. A degree, money, connections, permission.
They didn't. They picked something and started.
Today you pick yours: a path, a name and one line about what you do. Tomorrow your site gets built from it.

steps.title: Say it in one line.
steps.body: What you do and who it's for, the way you'd text it to a friend.

days.label: DAY 3 OF 14 · YOUR OFFER
days.headline: One line. Who, result, how, price.
days.line: Make the offer so good it feels almost too good to be true.

steps.title: Write one line.
steps.body: Who it's for, the result they get, how you do it, and the price.

steps.title: Get it graded.
steps.body: The grade shows which part is weakest.

steps.title: Fix one thing and re-grade.
steps.body: Usually it's the result: make it something they'd say out loud.

steps.title: Put it on your site.
steps.body: It goes in the big line at the top.

blocks.text: Before: "Car detailing services." After: "Your car, cleaned inside and out in your driveway while you work, $89."
Jordan posted both lines and asked which one people would buy. Seven comments, all for the second one.

intro: Your site is up. Right now it says what you do. Today it says why someone should say yes.
One line. Get it graded, fix the weakest part, and put it on your site.

blocks.label: The formula
blocks.text: I help [who] get [result] by [how], for [price].
Only promise a result you can deliver every time.
Grade my offer
Three examples:

items: Service: "Your car, cleaned inside and out in your driveway in 2 hours, $89."
Products: "A portrait of your dog, hand-painted from one photo, framed and shipped in 10 days, $65."
Creator or skill: "3 short videos of real customers using your product, delivered in 7 days, $150."

stuck.q: I don't know what to charge.
stuck.a: Pick a price a friend would pay without thinking, then add 20%. Monday is price day, so you can change it then.
Good. The grade tells you which part to fix. Fix one part and grade it again.
Say what they'd tell a friend afterwards. "My car looks new" beats "premium detailing".

days.headline: Show it's real.
days.line: People believe what they can see.
intro: An offer on its own is a promise. Proof makes it real.
Today you add one piece of proof to your site: a before and after, photos of your work, a sample or a mockup. Nothing yet? Make it on yourself, a friend or your own stuff.
days.move_time: about 15 minutes, plus the time to do the job if you're making your proof today

steps.title: Pick one kind of proof.
steps.body: Whatever you can make today:
sub: Photos of your work, or of you doing it
A sample: a free first one for a friend
A mockup, if it isn't made yet

steps.title: Make it.
steps.body: Your phone is enough. Daylight and a plain background.

steps.title: Add it to your site.
steps.body: Right under your offer.

blocks.text: For a service:

items: A before and after on your own car, room or yard
A short video of you doing the work
A friend's honest line about the result, with their OK

blocks.text: For products:

items: The product on a plain background, in daylight
It in use, in someone's hands
A mockup if it isn't made yet, labeled as a mockup

blocks.text: For a creator or skill:

items: A 30-second sample of what you'd make
A before and after of something you edited or taught
Your best post so far

blocks.text: Only use someone's words or photo with their OK. Never make up a review.
If they're a friend or got it free, say so next to their words, like "Free first detail for a friend."
Coaching on health, weight or skin? Skip the before and after.
Jordan detailed his own car Thursday night and shot it from the same spot before and after. Two photos, side by side, right under his offer.

stuck.q: I don't have anything to show yet.
stuck.a: Make it on yourself. Your own car, your own room, your own first product. It still counts.
Shoot by a window in daylight, against a plain wall. A phone is fine.

stuck.q: Can I use a photo from the internet?
stuck.a: No. Use your own, or a mockup you made and call it a mockup.

Then it's probably close. Keep it this week and see what people say.

intro: You don't need a big following to start. You need a short list of people who could use what you do.

blocks.text: Find local businesses

Open the brand list
Three messages to copy:

blocks.label: Someone you know
blocks.text: Hey [name], I just started [business]: [offer line]. You came to mind. Would you or someone you know want it? Here's the site: [link]

blocks.label: Book it
blocks.text: Hey [name], I just opened [business]. I've got 3 spots this week for [offer line]. Want one? Here's the site: [link]
Only say how many spots you have if it's true.

blocks.label: Free first one
blocks.text: Hey [name], I'm starting [business] and I'm doing the first few free in exchange for honest feedback. Want one?

blocks.text: Hey [name], I'm taking the first orders for [product] this week. [offer line]. Want me to save you one?
Send these one at a time from your own account. Don't use tools that mass-text or auto-DM people.

If anyone pays you, be ready to deliver what you promised by the date you gave, or refund them right away. If you pre-sell physical products, the FTC's Mail Order Rule requires shipping within the time you state (or 30 days) or offering a refund.
Jordan sent 5. Two didn't answer, one said not now, one asked for a price for two cars, and one booked a Saturday.

stuck.a: Send the first one in the next 5 minutes. The second is easier.
Replies take a day or two. Tomorrow you follow up once. Zero replies still counts as done.
Agree the date and the price in writing, then do a great job. That's your first story.

intro: Tomorrow night is demo night. I'll go through real sites live on Instagram.
Today you record a 60-second walkthrough: your site on screen, who it's for, what they get and one thing you learned. Post it, and tick the box below if you want to be considered for demo night.

steps.title: Screen-record your site.
steps.body: Scroll slowly from top to bottom.

steps.title: Talk over it.
steps.body: Who it's for, what they get, the price, and one thing you learned.

steps.title: Post it.
steps.body: Story, feed or Close Friends. Tag @buildwith127 and #DayOne127 if you like. You don't need to, to be considered for demo night.

blocks.label: Walkthrough
blocks.text: This is [business]. I help [who] get [result]. You get [package] for [price]. Two weeks ago it didn't exist. One thing I learned: [lesson].
Your face is optional. A voice over the screen, or just captions, is fine.
Jordan recorded his walkthrough on the couch in one take, 52 seconds, and posted it to his story.

stuck.a: Everyone does. Use captions with no voice instead.
Cut the intro. Start with the name of your business.

days.label: DAY 14 OF 14 · DEMO NIGHT
days.headline: Two weeks ago it didn't exist.
intro: Look at what you made: a name, a site, an offer with proof, a package, a list, a public post, asks sent and followed up.
Today: write down what you learned, and come to demo night at 8pm ET. I'll go through real sites live and show you what opens tomorrow.

steps.title: Write your one line.
steps.body: What you learned in two weeks.

steps.title: Count it up.
steps.body: Asks and replies across the challenge. Real numbers. Zero counts.

steps.title: Come to demo night.
steps.body: 8pm ET on Instagram, @elichristiansen_.

blocks.text: Add demo night to my calendar

If anyone pays you, be ready to deliver what you promised by the date you gave, or refund them right away. If you pre-sell physical products, the FTC's Mail Order Rule requires shipping within the time you state (or 30 days) or offering a refund.
Jordan's line: "I waited a year for the perfect idea. Two weeks of doing beat it."

stuck.a: Any 12 of the 14 count as finishing. Check in on the days you did by 11:59pm ET tonight.
The replay goes up on your challenge page after it airs.
